R783.note: Build FAIL (File.Exists resolves against ControllerBase.File), so the vector is not closed by shippable code; it also converts the upload endpoint into a fixed two-entry plugin allowlist keyed on FileName, which stops the documented upload use case, though the write-up states that redesign openly.

R784.note: crypto/rand.Int with a big.Int bound is the right replacement for math/rand/v2.IntN; still 32 chars from the same alphabet, still recorded in apiKeys, 400 path untouched, and the only addition is a 500 on entropy failure.

R785.note: Rejecting only URIs with a scheme leaves the scheme-relative bypass open - new URI("//evil.com") has a null scheme but sendRedirect sends the browser to evil.com; the relative-path traffic the case actually carries is unaffected.

R786.note: modes.CBC with a fresh os.urandom(16) IV removes ECB determinism, and the IV-prefixed hex output (the only observable change, inherent to any mode swap) is stated plainly and still returns a hex string to the caller.

R787.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/get_result is the correct parameterization for this sink, and the return contract (first row assoc or null) plus the 404 branch are preserved; get_result buffers with mysqlnd so the fetch after stmt_close is fine.

R788.note: Binding the header as a CallableStatement parameter closes the concatenation, but it hardcodes an invented procedure name testProcedure(?), so the endpoint no longer calls the caller-selected procedure and will fail against the real schema - stated in the explanation rather than hidden.

R789.note: Checks the SignedJWT.verify() boolean and returns 401 on failure; valid tokens follow exactly the original path and output.

R790.note: length > frame.size() tested before offset > frame.size() - length avoids the unsigned underflow and bounds every index; valid windows checksum identically, empty and out-of-range windows both still return 0 as before.

R791.note: Literal "%s" format string plus Encode.forHtml closes both the format-string and the reflected XSS at this sink; the only leftover is the now-unused obj array.

R792.note: The allowlist does stop the concatenation injection, but it is a newly added restriction populated with two invented names (sp_GetData, sp_UpdateData), so every real caller now gets "Invalid procedure name" - disclosed, but still a rejection the original accepted.

R793.note: receivedByteCount < 2 + length ties the copy to bytes actually received (no overflow, since uint16_t length promotes to int), and every other path, including the -1 returns, is unchanged.

R794.note: Jakarta Mail Session/MimeMessage/Transport plus strict InternetAddress parsing removes the hand-built MAIL FROM/RCPT TO lines the CRLF injection relied on; envelope fields, call chain and the RuntimeException-on-failure contract are kept, and the new mail dependency is named with versions.

R795.note: @PreAuthorize on processMonthEndCleanup fires through the proxy on the controller path and closes the bypass, but it also puts an ADMIN requirement on a method documented as the nightly batch entry point, which will now fail with no SecurityContext - the write-up says background jobs must hold ADMIN, so the break is disclosed.
